<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par150" /><!-- continued from the previous page -->{{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲנֵלֵךְ אִם <ref>On the use of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} in deliberative questions, see {{GHGpar|107|t}}; on the ''perfectum confidentiae'' in interrogative sentences, see {{GHGpar|106|n}}.</ref>נֶחְדָּ֑ל}} ''shall we go... or shall we forbear?'' Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אָן|translate=where? whither?}} {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נָה|translate=whither}}, and J. Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Sprachwiss. Untersuchungen}}, i. 13 ff.

The particular uses are as follows:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|d}}
(''a'') The particle {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} stands primarily before the simple question, when the questioner is wholly uncertain as to the answer to be expected, and may be used either before noun-clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הַעוֹד אֲבִיכֶם חַי הֲיֵשׁ לָכֶם אָח|translate=is your father yet alive? have ye}} another ''brother?'' for {{GHGheb|text=הֲיֵשׁ}} cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=11}}; for {{GHGheb|text=הֲכִי|translate=is it that?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=22}}; for {{GHGheb|text=הֲכִי יֶשׁ־|translate=is there yet?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=9|verse=1}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=19}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֲכִי}} read {{GHGheb|text=הִנּוֹ}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=25}}); for {{GHGheb|text=הַאֵין|translate=is there not?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=7}}, &c.; or before verbal-clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=3}} ''hast thou considered'' ({{GHGheb|text=הֲשַׂ֫מְתָּ לִבְּךָ}}) ''my servant Job?'' In other cases {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} (= ''num?'') is used before questions, to which, from their tone and contents, a negative answer is expected, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=14}} ''if a man die'', {{GHGheb|text=הֲיִחְֽיֶה|translate=shall he}} indeed ''live'' again? Sometimes a question is so used only as a rhetorical form instead of a negative assertion, or of a surprised or indignant refusal,<ref>Analogous to this is the use of the interrogative {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} in the sense of a reproachful remonstrance instead of a prohibition, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=מַה־תָּעִירוּ|translate=why should ye stir up?}} i.e. ''pray, stir not up''; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=1}}; see above, § 148.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתָּה תִבְנֶה־לִּי בַיִת|translate=shalt thou build me an house?}} (in the parallel passage {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=17|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אַתָּה וג׳|translate=thou shalt not}}, &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲשֹׁמֵר אָחִי אָנֹ֫כִי}} ''am I my brother’s keeper?'' cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=7}}, and the two passages where {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} is used before the infinitive ({{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=18}}, {{GHGterm|absol.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=2}}; on both, see § 113 ee, with the note).—On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=31}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֲנָקֵל}} (after {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}}) read {{GHGheb|text=הַנָּקֵל}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|e}}
Rem. 1. A few passages deserve special mention, in which the use of the interrogative is altogether different from our idiom, since it serves merely to express the conviction that the contents of the statement are well known to the hearer, and are unconditionally admitted by him. Thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=11}} ''surely thou hast eaten''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲכִי קָרָא}} prop. ''is it so that one names?'' &c., i.e. ''of a truth he is rightly named Jacob''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=15}} ''verily thou art my brother''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=6}}, I S 2:27 ''I did indeed'', &c.; 20:37, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=3}} ''ye know surely...''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=4}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=19}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=54|verse=2}}) a surprising communication is introduced in this way (by {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא}}) in order to show it to be absolutely true, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=7}} a concession is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=הֲלוֹא|translate=I have, it is true}}, &c. Finally, we may include the formula of quotation {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא הִיא כְתוּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=13}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא־הֵם כְּתוּבִים}} equivalent to ''surely it is, they are'' written (the latter in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, and very often elsewhere in the books of Kings and Chronicles), synonymous with the simple formula of assertion {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה כְתוּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=18}}, and {{GHGheb|text=הִנָּם כְּתוּבִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=15|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=27|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=32|hidebook=1}}.

Of very frequent occurrence also are questions introduced by {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}}, which really contain an affirmation and are used to state the reason for a request or warning, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=22}} ''turn thee aside... wherefore should I smite thee to the ground?'' i.e. ''otherwise I will'' (or ''must'') ''smite'', &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=17}}, and Driver on the passage; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=16}}; also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=12}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=79|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=115|verse=2|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=10}}.<section end="par150" /><noinclude>
